vulnerability_analysis: The contract has an owner-only function sumBounsPiece() that allows setting dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] to any arbitrary value. When users call receiveBounsToken(), the _sumCanGetToken() function multiplies dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] by balancePiece and subtracts from dayPoolBouns[yesToday]. Setting dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] to a very large value (e.g., type(uint256).max) will cause an underflow when users try to claim rewards, effectively locking all bonus distributions.
attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner, get yesterday's date string (yesToday), call sumBounsPiece() with an extremely large value to set dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday], then verify that dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] > dayPoolBouns[yesToday] which will cause underflow in reward distribution.
step_by_step_plan:
1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the contract owner
2. Get the yesToday date string using getDays() function
3. Call sumBounsPiece(yesToday, type(uint256).max) as owner
4. Verify oracle condition: dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] > dayPoolBouns[yesToday]
5. Optionally demonstrate that receiveBounsToken() reverts for a user
